newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Distant kin of late N.Korean leader defects - Seoul.
newsitem.headline: Distant kin of late N.Korean leader defects - Seoul.

text.p: Two North Korean families, including a distant relative of the Stalinist state's late leader Kim Il-sung, defected to South Korea by sea on Wednesday, the state Agency for National Security Planning said.
The agency said in a statement that among the eight defectors was Kim Young-jin, a relative by marriage to Kim Il-sung's wife.
The eight sought political asylum after entering South Korean waters in the Yellow Sea.

The defectors, rescued by South Korean maritime police, were due to arrive at the port of Inchon, just west of Seoul. The agency did not give any further details but Yonhap television news earlier reported they made the journey in a small boat.
An increasing number of North Koreans have fled the country and sought asylum in the South following several years of chronic food shortages.
